dz.$description:
Comfortable density: for touch, for a general audience, and for anything a person uses occasionally rather than all day. Apply on a container:
…
(composes with .arena-light and with a design extension) The counterpart to density.compact.json, and the reason target size is density's axis and never an extension's: how large a control is answers who is pointing at it, not what voice the product is speaking in. A shop on a phone and a console on a desk can want the same extension and opposite densities, and only separate axes let them have that. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with .arena-compact. Both set the same keys, so a container wearing both gets whichever the stylesheet emits last, which is a question nobody should have to ask. The text ladder deliberately does not move. Compact shrinks it because an expert reading a dense table is trading legibility for how much fits; comfortable has nothing to buy with the same trade, so the box grows and the words stay the size they were.

ctl-h.$description:
48px clears WCAG 2.5.8's enhanced 44px target, which the 40px base does not,
and that is the whole point of this file: the base meets the 24px minimum and this meets the
one a thumb actually wants.
